newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SELES INTO SEMIFINALS, SAMPRAS INTO QUARTERFINALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES INTO SEMIFINALS, SAMPRAS INTO QUARTERFINALS.

text.p: Playing in her first tournament of the year, fourth seed Monica Seles is through to the Lipton Championships semifinals after winning a 3-6 6-2 6-3 quarterfinal battle on Tuesday over seventh seed Irina Spirlea of Romania.
Seles is into her 62nd semifinal in 80 career tournaments played. To date, she's won 38 titles, including nine Grand Slam laurels.
But the lack of recent match play the past few months finds Seles a little off-balance.
"I still don't feel I have the confidence I should," Seles said. "I wasn't sure how I'm going to play physically and mentally."
Seles meets 11th seed Barbara Paulus of Austria in the semis. The 14th-ranked Paulus defeated Sadrine Testud of France 6-3 6-3 in the other quarterfinal played on Tuesday.
In men's fourth round action, top seed Pete Sampras of the United States, second seed Thomas Muster of Austria and fourth seed Goran Ivanisevic of Croatia moved into the quarterfinals.
The top-ranked Sampras spoiled 45th-ranked Magnus Larsson's 27th birthday by downing the Swede 6-2 6-0 in 56-minutes.
"I really played unbelievable tennis for the most part," Sampras said. "I served well, got off to a good start. It was a smooth day, a real good day."
Successfully turning back 22nd-ranked Alex Corretja of Spain, the second-ranked Muster won a 6-4 6-4 encounter.
It was a 6-4 6-4 victory for the fifth-ranked Ivanisevic over 61st-ranked Dominik Hrbaty of Slovakia, recently named the ATP Tour Newcomer of the Year.
Other fourth round winners were Sergi Bruguera of Spain, Jonas Bjorkman of Sweden, Hendrik Dreekman of Germany and Andre Medvedev of the Ukraine.
The 29th-ranked Bjorkman bypassed hard-serving Mark Philippoussis of Australia, who twisted his ankle early on in the match, with a 6-3 6-4 win.
Seles, a Yugoslavian-born, naturalised American, won back-to-back titles at The Lipton in 1990 and 1991 and has a 20-2 record at this tournament.
A broken index finger's kept Seles on the sidelines until now, but experience and determination is helping her win matches.

"Obviously, the way I played today, I need a little more consistency," Seles admitted. "I could hit some nice shots, then I could just drop. I had a hard time closing out a couple of key games. That, I think, is a lack of match play."

If there was any bright factor to the day for the ninth-ranked Spirlea, who recently reached the final at Indian Wells, it was that she finally won a set off of Seles. In their three previous encounters, Seles won all six sets played.
Seles started the match with a 2-0 lead, but Spirlea used her crunching forehand and slice backhand to win the next five games en route to taking the first set.
After dropping her serve in the opening game of the second set, Seles won the next eight points. A service break in the sixth game put her on the way to a second set win.

In the final set showdown, Seles took what appeared to be a commanding 4-1 lead. But Spirlea came back and was serving to even the score at 4-all. A netted forehand at 30-40, however, put Seles at 5-3 and serving for the match.

Sampras, who now has a 5-1 winning record over Larsson, has won three of the four tournaments he's entered this year, including the Australian Open. His match record for the year is an impressive 20-1.
While Sampras never lost his serve in the match, Larsson only held serve twice in the match, in the first and fifth games of the first set.
